purpose: Follow-up robustness evidence for historical backfill, enrichment, and state-change wording variants; API completion is not a semantic accuracy score.

observations.historical_backfill: All three historical/backfill phrasings created a separate dated MySQL memory and left the current PostgreSQL memory unchanged. Historical and current queries selected the expected record.
observations.enrichment: Both preference-enrichment phrasings used UPDATE and merged the added detail into the existing memory, retaining both user source IDs.
observations.state_change: Both state-change phrasings created a new current record and linked the old record with superseded_by. Current and previous-state queries selected the expected record.

limits: This is one real-model run on synthetic wording variants, not a benchmark or proof of general accuracy.
The runner used vector-only candidate retrieval because optional FastEmbed/spaCy components were not installed.
The run does not establish reliable point-in-time knowledge reconstruction; that remains a separate provenance/history requirement.
